accepted.s: With regard to constitutional amendments requiring ratification by the States, which one of the following is correct?
o: Ratification by not less than half of the State Legislatures by a special majority is required.
Ratification by not less than half of the State Legislatures by a simple majority is required.
Ratification by all State Legislatures by a two-thirds majority is required.
Ratification by a majority of the State Legislatures and approval through referendums is required.
accepted.x: An amendment affecting specified federal provisions must be ratified by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States, using a simple majority in each Legislature.
accepted.tq: Separate the proportion of States from the kind of majority required in each Legislature.
accepted.sec: ■ Provisions requiring state ratification - list, proportion, role of State Legislature  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding State ratification of a Constitution Amendment Bill is correct?
o: The Constitution prescribes a definite period within which every State must communicate its decision.
Ratification may be done by a simple majority of the members present and voting in each concerned State Legislature.
Ratification must be approved by the Governor before it becomes valid.
A State Legislature may initiate an amendment relating to any federal provision.
accepted.x: State ratification is by simple majority of each concerned State Legislature, and no time limit is prescribed. States cannot initiate constitutional amendments.
accepted.tq: Check separately the majority, time-limit and initiating authority instead of treating ratification as a single step.
accepted.sec: ■ Provisions requiring state ratification - list, proportion, role of State Legislature  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following subjects requires ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States for its constitutional amendment?
1. Election of the President and the manner of that election
2. Representation of States in Parliament
3. Distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States
4. Citizenship
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The election of the President, representation of States in Parliament and distribution of legislative powers are federal provisions requiring State ratification. Citizenship is amended by simple majority outside Article 368.
accepted.tq: Identify the federal provisions first and reject the ordinary-law subject mixed into the list.
accepted.sec: ■ Provisions requiring state ratification - list, proportion, role of State Legislature  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

List-I: Constitutional subject
A. Election of the President
B. GST Council
C. Representation of States in Parliament
D. Citizenship

List-II: Provision
1. Article 279A
2. Articles 54 and 55
3. Fourth Schedule
4. Article 11

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Articles 54 and 55 concern the election of the President; Article 279A establishes the GST Council; the Fourth Schedule concerns representation of States in Parliament; Article 11 concerns citizenship.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure article-subject pairs and eliminate codes containing a misplaced provision.
accepted.sec: ■ Provisions requiring state ratification - list, proportion, role of State Legislature  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was added to the category of provisions requiring State ratification by the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016?
accepted.x: The 101st Amendment Act, 2016 added Article 279A relating to the GST Council to the federal provisions requiring State ratification.
accepted.tq: Use the amendment-year association and distinguish the GST Council from other constitutional bodies.
accepted.sec: ■ Provisions requiring state ratification - list, proportion, role of State Legislature  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the role of State Legislatures in constitutional amendment?
o: A State Legislature may refer an amendment Bill to the Supreme Court for approval.
A State Legislature cannot initiate a constitutional amendment; it can only ratify certain Bills passed by Parliament.
A State Legislature can initiate an amendment by passing a resolution under Article 368.
A State Legislature can introduce an amendment Bill in Parliament concerning a State subject.
accepted.x: States cannot initiate amendments under Article 368. Their role is limited to ratifying amendments concerning specified federal provisions; the creation or abolition of a Legislative Council follows Article 169 outside Article 368.
accepted.tq: Ask who has the initiating power and distinguish it from the State Legislature’s limited ratifying role.
accepted.sec: ■ Provisions requiring state ratification - list, proportion, role of State Legislature  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court’s decision in Rajendra N. Shah (2021) is associated with which of the following?
o: Striking down Part IXB in its entirety for violating the federal structure without any further qualification
Invalidating the GST Council under Article 279A
Declaring the 24th Amendment unconstitutional for abridging Fundamental Rights
Striking down the provisions relating to State co-operative societies in Part IXB for want of ratification by the States
accepted.x: In Rajendra N. Shah (2021), the provisions of Part IXB relating to State co-operative societies were struck down for want of ratification by the required number of States.
accepted.tq: Match the judgment with the precise constitutional defect rather than the broad subject of federalism.
accepted.sec: ■ Provisions requiring state ratification - list, proportion, role of State Legislature  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following amendments to the Constitution can be made by Parliament by a simple majority and is not treated as an amendment under Article 368?
1. Formation of new States and alteration of their areas, boundaries or names
2. Creation or abolition of Legislative Councils in States
3. Change in the official language under Article 343
4. Amendment of the basic structure of the Constitution
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Formation and alteration of States, Legislative Councils and official language provisions are among matters amendable by simple majority outside Article 368. The basic structure cannot be amended even by the special procedure.
accepted.tq: Spot the impermissible constitutional concept mixed with provisions amendable by ordinary law.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendments by simple majority outside Article 368 - which provisions  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a provision that may be amended by a simple majority outside Article 368?
o: The distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States
The number of puisne judges of the Supreme Court
accepted.x: The distribution of legislative powers, including the Seventh Schedule, is a federal provision requiring the prescribed State ratification. Citizenship, the Fifth and Sixth Schedules and the number of puisne judges of the Supreme Court are amendable by simple majority.
accepted.tq: Find the federal provision that does not belong to the ordinary-law category.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendments by simple majority outside Article 368 - which provisions  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 2 to Article 4 — Formation and alteration of States
Article 169 — Creation or abolition of Legislative Councils
accepted.x: Article 368 contains the general constitutional amendment procedure, whereas citizenship is among the matters that can be changed by simple majority under Article 11. Articles 2–4, 169 and 327 relate to the subjects stated.
accepted.tq: Use the wrong Article-subject pairing trap and verify the provision against the subject.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendments by simple majority outside Article 368 - which provisions  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following matters is included among those that can be changed by simple majority outside Article 368?
1. Quorum in Parliament
2. Salaries and emoluments of Members of Parliament
3. Privileges of Parliament and its members
4. The basic structure of the Constitution
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Parliamentary quorum, salaries of MPs and parliamentary privileges are among provisions amendable by simple majority outside Article 368. The basic structure is beyond the amending power.
accepted.tq: Group the parliamentary procedural and administrative matters, then eliminate the basic-structure proposition.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendments by simple majority outside Article 368 - which provisions  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the method of amendment?
o: Representation of States in Parliament — simple majority outside Article 368
Official language — special majority under Article 368 only
GST Council — simple majority as an ordinary law
accepted.x: Citizenship under Article 11 is amendable by simple majority outside Article 368. The GST Council and representation of States in Parliament are among provisions requiring State ratification.
accepted.tq: Compare the ordinary-law category with the federal-ratification category rather than relying on the subject’s importance.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendments by simple majority outside Article 368 - which provisions  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following provisions in the order in which they are referred to in the Constitution, from the earliest Article number to the latest:
A. Creation or abolition of Legislative Councils
B. Citizenship
C. Elections and delimitation
D. Official language
accepted.x: The relevant provisions are Article 11 for citizenship, Article 169 for Legislative Councils, Article 327 for elections and delimitation, and Article 343 for official language.
accepted.tq: Order the items by Article number, not by the political importance of the subject.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendments by simple majority outside Article 368 - which provisions  [other exams]

accepted.s: The power of Parliament to amend Fundamental Rights was constitutionally affirmed in response to which judicial decision by the Constitution (24th Amendment) Act, 1971?
accepted.x: The 24th Amendment Act, 1971 was enacted in response to Golaknath (1967), which had restricted Parliament’s power to amend Fundamental Rights.
accepted.tq: Link the constitutional amendment to the judgment it was designed to answer.
accepted.sec: ■ Limitations - basic structure, 24th Amendment, judicial review of amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s: What was the effect of the Constitution (24th Amendment) Act, 1971 on Articles 13 and 368?
o: It declared every constitutional amendment to be ordinary law under Article 13.
It empowered Parliament to amend Fundamental Rights and inserted Article 13(4), excluding an Article 368 amendment from the term ‘law’ in Article 13.
It prohibited Parliament from amending Fundamental Rights and removed Article 368.
It made all constitutional amendments subject to approval by a national referendum.
accepted.x: The 24th Amendment amended Articles 13 and 368, empowered Parliament to abridge or take away Fundamental Rights and inserted Article 13(4), under which an amendment made under Article 368 is not ‘law’ for Article 13.
accepted.tq: Test the paired effects of one amendment instead of confusing it with the later basic-structure judgments.
accepted.sec: ■ Limitations - basic structure, 24th Amendment, judicial review of amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kesavananda Bharati judgment upheld the 24th Amendment.
2. The judgment held that Fundamental Rights and the Preamble cannot be amended under any circumstances.
3. The judgment held that the basic structure cannot be altered by constitutional amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Kesavananda Bharati upheld the 24th Amendment and held that the basic structure cannot be amended. It also held that Fundamental Rights and the Preamble are amendable, subject to the basic-structure limitation.
accepted.tq: Separate amendability of individual provisions from the unamendability of the basic structure.
accepted.sec: ■ Limitations - basic structure, 24th Amendment, judicial review of amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The amending power of Parliament is not unlimited.
Reason (R): The basic structure of the Constitution cannot be altered even by a constitutional amendment.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the basic-structure limitation directly explains why Parliament’s constituent amending power is not unlimited.
accepted.tq: Check whether the Reason supplies the constitutional basis for the limitation stated in the Assertion.
accepted.sec: ■ Limitations - basic structure, 24th Amendment, judicial review of amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s:
The Constitution (42nd Amendment) Act, 1976 attempted to achieve which of the following in relation to the amending power?
1. To declare the amending power unlimited
2. To make constitutional amendments non-justiciable
3. To insert clauses (4) and (5) in Article 368
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The 42nd Amendment inserted clauses (4) and (5) in Article 368, declared the amending power unlimited and attempted to bar judicial review of constitutional amendments.
accepted.tq: Treat the amendment number, clauses and legal effect as separate checks in a statement question.
accepted.sec: ■ Limitations - basic structure, 24th Amendment, judicial review of amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of the Minerva Mills judgment, 1980?
o: It struck down the provisions making the amending power unlimited and excluding judicial review.
It declared the 24th Amendment wholly unconstitutional.
It upheld clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 as valid limitations on judicial review.
It held that the Preamble could not be amended.
accepted.x: Minerva Mills struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 inserted by the 42nd Amendment. It reaffirmed that limited amending power and judicial review are basic features.
accepted.tq: Match the judgment with the precise provision it invalidated, not with the earlier Golaknath dispute.
accepted.sec: ■ Limitations - basic structure, 24th Amendment, judicial review of amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following expressions is used in Article 368 to describe Parliament’s constituent power to amend the Constitution?
o: May, in exercise of its judicial power, interpret or repeal any provision
Shall, in exercise of its constituent power, amend every provision by referendum
May, in exercise of its constituent power, amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision
May, in exercise of its legislative power, repeal only those provisions approved by the States
accepted.x: Article 368 states that Parliament may, in exercise of its constituent power, amend the Constitution by way of addition, variation or repeal of any provision, subject to the basic-structure limitation.
accepted.tq: Select the precise constitutional wording and reject substitutions of legislative or judicial power.
accepted.sec: ■ Limitations - basic structure, 24th Amendment, judicial review of amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s: The amendment procedure of the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from which country?
accepted.x: The amendment procedure of the Indian Constitution is generally identified as having been borrowed from South Africa.
accepted.tq: Use the source-country association specific to the amendment procedure rather than the source of another constitutional feature.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendment procedure → source country and criticism

accepted.s: Which one of the following best characterises the nature of the Indian constitutional amendment procedure?
o: It is entirely flexible because every provision can be changed by ordinary law.
It is rigid only in matters relating to Fundamental Rights.
It is a synthesis of rigidity and flexibility.
It is entirely rigid because every provision requires State ratification.
accepted.x: The Indian Constitution combines different methods of amendment and is therefore neither purely rigid nor purely flexible; it is a synthesis of both.
accepted.tq: Compare the constitutional system as a whole instead of applying one amendment method to every provision.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendment procedure → source country and criticism

accepted.s: Who described the constitutional amendment process as appearing ‘complicated’ but being ‘merely diverse’?
accepted.x: Granville Austin described the process as appearing complicated but being merely diverse. He also called it one of the most ably conceived aspects of the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the constitutional scholar associated with the exact evaluative description.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendment procedure → source country and criticism

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a criticism commonly made of the constitutional amendment procedure in India?
o: A joint sitting is available to resolve a deadlock between the two Houses on an amendment Bill.
There is no time limit for State ratification.
There is no special constitutional body or referendum for amendments.
accepted.x: The Constitution provides no joint sitting mechanism for resolving a deadlock between the Houses on an amendment Bill. The other three are recognised criticisms of the procedure.
accepted.tq: Look for the proposition that reverses an actual criticism by asserting that a safeguard exists.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendment procedure → source country and criticism

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding criticisms of the constitutional amendment procedure:
1. Parliament alone can amend most constitutional provisions.
2. No outside constitutional convention or special body is required for amendment.
3. Ratification by the States is required for every constitutional amendment.
4. States cannot initiate an amendment under Article 368.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Parliament alone amends most provisions, no special body or referendum is required, and States cannot initiate amendments. State ratification is required only for a limited group of federal provisions, not every amendment.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute statement ‘every’ by distinguishing limited State ratification from general amendment practice.
accepted.sec: ■ Amendment procedure → source country and criticism

accepted.s: A constitutional amendment Bill affecting the representation of States in Parliament has been passed by Parliament. Which further constitutional requirement applies before it can be presented for Presidential assent?
o: Approval by a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament
Approval by all State Legislatures through special majority
Ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States by simple majority
A referendum held in the affected States only
accepted.x: Representation of States in Parliament is a federal provision. Its amendment requires ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States by simple majority; no joint sitting or referendum is prescribed.
accepted.tq: Apply the federal-provision test to the facts of the proposed amendment.
accepted.sec: ■ Provisions requiring state ratification - list, proportion, role of State Legislature  [other exams]
